x: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of His saying N. Some of them said: It is the whale on which the earths rest.
It was mentioned by the one who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The first thing that God created was the pen, so it wrote what would be, then He raised the water vapor, and from it the heavens were created, then He created the letter Nun, and the earth was spread out on the back of the letter Nun, so the earth moved and swayed, and it was fixed by the mountains, for the mountains boast of the earth. He said: And he recited: Nun, by the pen
h
and what they write

c: Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us: Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan,
m: or Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Abbas, in a similar manner, except that he said: Then the heavens were split from it.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya told us: Sufyan told us: Sulayman told us, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: “The first thing that God created was the pen. He said: Write. He said: What should I write? He said: Write the destiny. He said: So it wrote what would happen from that day until the Hour of Resurrection. Then He created the Nun and raised the water vapor, so the heavens burst forth from it and the earth was spread out on the back of the Nun. The Nun was compelled, so the earth shook, and He established the mountains, so they boast of being above the earth.” Wasil ibn Abd al-A'la narrated:

c: Muhammad ibn Fadil narrated to us, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The first thing that God created was the pen. Then He said to it: Write. It said: What should I write? It said: Write the destiny. He said: So the pen wrote down what would happen until the Day of Resurrection. Then He lifted up the water vapor and split the heavens from it. Then He created the nun, and the earth was spread out on its back. The nun was compelled, and the earth shook, and it was fixed with the mountains, and they boast over the earth.

c: Wasil bin Abdul A’la told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, that Ibrahim bin Abi Bakr told him on the authority of Mujahid, he said: It was said: The Nun is the whale that is under the seventh earth.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, he said: Muammar said: Al-A’mash told us, that Ibn Abbas said:
m: The first thing created was the pen. Then he mentioned a hadith similar to that of Wasil on the authority of Ibn Fadil, and he added to it: Then Ibn Abbas recited: “Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha Muslim ibn Subaih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The first thing my Lord created was the pen. He said to it: Write, so it wrote what will be until the Hour comes. Then He created the letter Nun above the water, then He pressed the earth down upon it.

x: Others said: N is one of the letters of the Most Gracious.
Who said that?

c: Abdullah bin Ahmed Al-Marwazi told us: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us: My father told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Alif, Lam, Meem, and Noon are the letters of the Most Gracious, separated.

c: Muhammad bin Muammar told me, he said: Abbas bin Ziyad al-Bahili told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement al-Raw, al-Ha-Mim, al-Nun, he said: It is a disjointed noun.

x: Others said: N is the inkwell, and al-Qalam is the pen.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Yaqub told us, he said: My brother Isa bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Thabit al-Bunani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: God created the nun, which is the inkwell, and created the pen, and said: Write, and it said: What should I write? He said: Write down what will happen until the Day of Resurrection, of deeds done, righteous or wicked, or the provision allocated, lawful or unlawful. Then He made obligatory for each thing its nature, its entry into the world and its duration in it, and its exit from it. Then He appointed guardians over the servants, and storers for the book. The guardians copy every day from the storers the work of that day. Then when the provision is exhausted and the trace is cut off, and the term expires, the guardians come to the storers asking for the work of that day. The storers say to them: We do not find anything for your companion with us. Then the storers return and find that they have died. Ibn Abbas said: Are you not an Arab people who hear the storers say: Indeed, we were copying what you did (al-Jathiyah 45:29). And can copying be anything other than from an original?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan and Qatada,
m: regarding his statement N, he said: It is the inkwell.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us: Amr told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: The letter nun means the inkwell.

x: Others said: N: a tablet of light.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Shabil Al-Maktab told us: Muhammad bin Ziyad Al-Jazari told us, on the authority of Furat bin Abi Al-Furat, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Farah, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe”: A tablet of light that records what will happen until the Day of Resurrection.

x: Others said: N is an oath that God swears by.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement, “Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe,” God swears by whatever He wills.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, “Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe,” he said: This is an oath by which God swore.

x: Others said: It is one of the names of the Surah.

Others said: It is a letter of the alphabet. We have already mentioned the statement regarding similar letters of the alphabet that begin the beginnings of the surahs, and the statement regarding his statement is similar to the statement regarding that. The reciters differed in the reading of Nun. The majority of the reciters of Kufa pronounced the nun in it and in Ya Seen, except for al-Kisa’i and the majority of the reciters of Basra, because it is a letter of the alphabet, and the alphabet is based on stopping on it even if it is connected. Al-Kisa’i would assimilate the last nun of them and conceal it based on the connection. The correct statement regarding this, in our view, is that they are two eloquent readings, and whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. However, the pronunciation of the letter nun is more eloquent and well-known, and I like it better. As for the pen, it is the well-known pen.
However, the pen by which our Lord swore was the pen that God, the Most High, created, and He commanded it to write down everything that will be until the Day of Resurrection.

c: Muhammad ibn Salih al-Anmati told me, saying: Ibad ibn al-Awam told us, saying: Abd al-Wahid ibn Salim told us, saying:
m: I heard Ata’ say: I asked al-Walid ibn Ubadah ibn al-Samit: What was your father’s last will and testament when death gathered him? He said: He called me and said: O my son, fear God, and know that you will never fear God and you will never attain knowledge until you believe in God alone and in destiny, both its good and its bad. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The first thing God created was the pen, and He said to it: Write. It said: O Lord, what should I write? He said: Write destiny. The pen wrote at that moment what was and what will be until eternity.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Tusi told me: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq told us: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us: Rabah ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Habib, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Or is it that God created the pen and commanded it to write down everything?

c: Musa bin Sahl al-Ramli told us: Na’im bin Hammad told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us
m: with his chain of transmission, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hashim, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: I said to Ibn Abbas: Some people lie about predestination. He said: They lie about the Book of God. I will take hold of one of their hairs and not cut it short. God was on His Throne before He created anything. The first thing He created was the pen, which recorded what would happen until the Day of Resurrection. People only act on a matter that has already been completed.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Samad told us: Shu’bah told us: Abu Hashim told us that
m: he heard Mujahid say: I heard Abdullah - we do not know whether it was Ibn Umar or Ibn Abbas - say: The first thing God created was the pen, and the pen wrote down what would happen. People today only work on what it has finished.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Muawiyah ibn Salih told me, and Abdullah ibn Adam told me, he said: My father told us, he said: Al-Layth ibn Saad told us, on the authority of Muawiyah ibn Salih, on the authority of Ayoub ibn Ziyad, he said: Ibad ibn al-Walid ibn al-Samit told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My father Ubadah ibn al-Samit said:
m: O my son, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The first thing God created was the pen, and He said to it: Write, and it wrote down in that instant what would happen until the Day of Resurrection.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, Nun and the pen, he said: that with which the remembrance was written.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said:
m: Surat al-Qalam 68:1 Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.

c: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh,
m: he told him on the authority of Ibrahim Ibn Abi Bakr, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Nun and the Pen, he said: That with which the remembrance was written. And his statement:
h
And what they write
means:
h
and what they write

and inscribe. If the interpretation is directed in this way, then the oath is by creation and their actions. The statement may have another meaning, which is that its meaning is: and they wrote what they write, so what is in the sense of a source. If the interpretation is directed in this way, then the oath is by the book, as if it was said: Nun, the pen, and the book. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And what they write
down he said:
h
And what they write
down.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
and what they write
, meaning: they write.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And what they write
, he said:
h
And what they write

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And what they write

down means what they write down. It is said from this: So-and-so wrote down the book, so he writes down a line: if he wrote it. And from this is the saying of Ru’bah ibn al-‘Ajaj: I and Astar wrote a line

evidence.text: The reciters differed in the reading of Nun.

The majority of the reciters of Kufa pronounced the nun in it and in Ya Seen, except for al-Kisa’i and the majority of the reciters of Basra, because it is a letter of the alphabet, and the alphabet is based on stopping on it even if it is connected.
The correct statement regarding this, in our view, is that they are two eloquent readings, and whichever one the reader recites, he is correct.

x: And His saying:
h
You are not
, by the grace of your Lord, a madman. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace:
h
You are not
, by the grace of your Lord, a madman, thereby disbelieving the polytheists of Quraysh who said to him: You are mad.

And His statement: And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted. God Almighty says: And indeed, O Muhammad, for you is a great reward from God for your patience in the face of the harm that the polytheists inflicted upon you, neither diminished nor cut off. This is from their saying: a weak rope, meaning it is weak. And its strength has weakened: meaning its strength has weakened.
Mujahid used to say about this:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, not grateful, he said: counted.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And indeed, O Muhammad, you are on a great path, and that is the path of the Qur’an with which God taught him, which is Islam and its laws. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, And indeed, you are of a great moral character, meaning: a great religion.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, And indeed, you are of a great moral character, meaning: You are of a great religion, which is Islam.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, a great creation, he said: religion.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: I asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: His character was the Qur’an, saying as it is in the Qur’an.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, And indeed, you are of a great moral character. It was mentioned to us that Saeed bin Hisham asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she said: Do you not read the Qur’an? He said: I said: Yes. She said: Indeed, the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the Qur’an.

c: Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas told us: My father told us: Al-Mubarak ibn Fadala told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Saeed ibn Hisham, who said:
m: I came to Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her, and I said: Tell me about the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: His character was the Qur’an. Do you not read: And indeed, you are of a great moral character?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Muawiyah ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Abu al-Zahariyyah, on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nufayl, he said:
m: So I went to Aisha and asked her about the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she said: The character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the Qur’an.

c: Ubaid bin Asbat told us: My father told me, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq, on the authority of Atiyah,
m: regarding his statement, And indeed, you are of a great moral character, he said: The etiquette of the Qur’an.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, regarding His statement,
h
He is of a great moral character
, meaning his religion and his affair that he was upon, from what he was commanded to do, from what God commanded him to do and entrusted him to.

x: And His statement,
h
Then you will see
, and they will see * which of you is afflicted. God Almighty says:
h
Then you will see
, O Muhammad, and the polytheists of your people who call you mad will see, which of you is afflicted. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
Then you will see
, and they will see, meaning: You will see, and they will see.

x: And his statement,
h
Which of you is the one who is afflicted
The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of that.

Some of them said: Its interpretation is which of you is the madman, as if he directed the meaning of the preposition with in his statement, with which of you to the meaning of in. And if you direct the preposition with to the meaning of in, then the interpretation of the statement is: And they see which of the two groups is the madman, in your group, O Muhammad, or their group. And the madman is a noun raised by the preposition with.
Mention of who said the meaning of that: Which of you is crazy?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Which of you is bewitched? He said: The insane. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid: Which of you is bewitched? He said: Which of you is insane.

x: Others said: Rather, the interpretation of that is: Which of you is crazy? It is as if those who said this statement directed the one who is being tempted to the meaning of temptation or temptations, just as it was said: He has no reason or conviction: meaning he has no mind or conviction of opinion. So in the same way, the one who is being tempted was placed in the place of temptations. It was mentioned that: The infatuated means the source and means madness.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Which of you is afflicted
? He said: Satan.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
Which of you is afflicted
? He meant madness.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: He says: Which of you is mad?

x: Rather, the meaning of this is: Which of you is more deserving of the devil? So, according to these people, the preposition ba is an addition, whether it enters or exits, and the example of these people is the saying of the rajaz poet: We are the Banu Ja'dah, the owners of the falaj. We strike with the sword and hope for relief.
Meaning: We hope for relief. For them, the inclusion of the letter ba in this position and its exclusion are the same.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then you will see
, and they will see *
h
Which of you is the one who is afflicted
, he said: Which of you is more deserving of the devil. The Arabists differed on this matter in the same way that the commentators differed.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The meaning of this is:
h
Then you will see
and they will see
h
which of you is the one who is afflicted
Some of the grammarians of Kufa said:
h
Which of you is afflicted

here, meaning madness, and it is in the doctrine of afflictions, as they said: It has no rational or binding basis. He said: If you wish, you can make which of you into which of you in which of the two groups is the madman. He said: In that case, it is a noun, not a source. The first and most correct of the sayings on this matter, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of that is: Which of you is mad? The direction of the one who is afflicted to the fitun in the sense of the source, because that is the most obvious meaning of the speech, if he did not intend to drop the ba’, and we made an understandable way for its inclusion, and we have explained that it is not permissible for there to be something in the Qur’an that has no meaning.

And His statement: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has gone astray from His way means, the Most High said: Indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, is most knowing of who has gone astray from His way, like the straying of the infidels of Quraysh from the religion of God and the path of guidance. And He is most knowing of the guided ones means: And He is most knowing of the guided ones, who followed the truth and acknowledged it, just as you were guided and followed the truth. This is from the metaphors of speech, but the meaning of the speech is: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing, O Muhammad, of you, and you are the guided one, and of your people from the infidels of Quraysh and that they are the ones who have gone astray from the path of truth.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So do not obey, O Muhammad, those who deny the signs of God and His Messenger. They wish that you would compromise so that they would compromise.
The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of this.
Some of them said: The meaning of this is: Those who deny the signs of God wish that you would disbelieve in God, O Muhammad, so that they would disbelieve.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
If you were to compromise
, they would be compliant, meaning: They would wish you would disbelieve, so they would disbelieve.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
They wish that you would compromise so that they would compromise
, that he said: You would disbelieve so that they would disbelieve.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan:
m: They wish you would compromise so they would compromise. He said: You would disbelieve so they would disbelieve.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: They would like you to make things easy for them so they would make things easy for them, or you would be lenient in your religion so they would be lenient in their religion.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
If you were to compromise
, they would compromise, meaning: If you were to make things easy for them, they would make things easy.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
They wish that you would compromise so they would compromise
, he said: If you were to give in to their gods and leave them some of the truth, they would be content with you.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
They wish that you would compromise so they would compromise
, meaning: They wish, O Muhammad, that you would compromise on this matter, so they would compromise with you.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
They wish that you would compromise so that they would compromise

, he said: They wish that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would compromise so that they would compromise. The more correct of the two opinions on this is the opinion of those who said: The meaning of this is: These polytheists, O Muhammad, would like you to be lenient with them in your religion by responding to their request to incline to their gods, so that they would be lenient with you in your worship of your God, as God Almighty said: “And had We not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined to them a little. Then We would have made you taste double the [expectation of] life and double the [expectation of] death.” It is taken from fat, similar to softening in the saying about softening of fat.

x: And his saying,
h
And do not obey every worthless swearer
. And do not obey, O Muhammad, every one who frequently swears falsely, worthless: he is weak.

The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that, except that some of them directed the meaning of humiliated to the liar, and I think that he did that because he saw that if he is described as humiliated, then he is only described with that because of the humiliation of his own soul that was upon him, and likewise the description of the liar, he only lies because of the humiliation of his own soul upon him.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And do not obey every worthless oath-taker. The worthless one is the liar.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, a humiliating oath-taker, he said: It is weak.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And do not obey every worthless swearer
, meaning one who commits many evil deeds.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of al-Hasan
m: regarding his statement,
h
Every oath-taker is despised
, he said: Every person who swears a lot is despised and weak.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of al-Hasan

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Qatada:
m: h
And do not obey every worthless swearer
. He said: He is the one who commits many evil deeds.

m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, a slanderer, he said: The slanderer is the one who slanders people with his hand and strikes them, but not with his tongue. He said: The obscene, vile person.” Muawiyah said, and I told Ayyadh bin Abdullah Al-Fahri, on the authority of Musa bin Uqbah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar to that.

h

h
He became a tyrant after

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin.
m: Al-Atal said: The correct and strong.

m: Abu Zakariya, who is Yahya bin Musʿab, told us on the authority of ʿUmar bin Nafiʿ, who said: ʿIkrimah was asked about Atal after that, a fornicator, and he said: That is the vile, infidel.

c: Ali bin Al-Hassan Al-Azdi told me that
m: Yahya, meaning Ibn Al-Yaman, told us on the authority of Abu Al-Ashhab on the authority of Al-Hassan regarding his statement, After that, he became a tyrant, he said: The obscene, mean, and vile person.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: The violent, mean, and obscene person.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, Atal, he said: Very evil.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: Atal He said: Atal means strong. “After that, a fornicator.” The meaning of after in this context is the meaning of with, and the interpretation of the statement is Atal after that and a fornicator: meaning with the fornicator. And his saying: Zanim and the Zanim in the speech of the Arabs: is the one who sticks to the people but is not one of them, and from it is the saying of Hassan bin Thabit: You are a bastard who has been hung on the Hashimites as a single cup is hung behind a rider.

x: Another said: A bastard who doesn't know who his father is, a prostitute of low birth And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Zanim he said:
m: The Zanim is the pretender, and it is said: The Zanim is a man who has a defect that he is known for, and it is said: He is Al-Akhns bin Shuraik Al-Thaqafi, an ally of Banu Zuhrah, and some people from Banu Zuhrah claimed that the Zanim is: Al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghuth Al-Zuhri, but he is not him.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: He is the adopted son.

m: that he heard him say about this verse:
h

m: The zanim is the one who is known for evil, just as a sheep is known by its hump, the one who sticks.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of the commentators, who said:
m: It is the one who has a tail like the tail of a sheep.

h

m: I heard Shahr bin Hawshab say: He is the coarse, the glutton and the drinker of what is forbidden.

Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, on the authority of Ibn Yaman, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin, who said:
m: The adulterer is a sign of the unbeliever.

c: Ibn Hamid told me: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin, who said:
m: The adulterer is a sign of the unbeliever.

m: The zaneem is the one who is known for his meanness, just as a sheep is known by its hump.

Who said that?

x: The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement if he was so Abu Jaʿfar al-Madani and Hamza recited it َأن كان ذ مالas a question with two hamzas, and those who recited it turned to two aspects: One of them is that it is intended to rebuke this humiliating oath-taker, so it was said: Because this humiliating oath-taker had wealth and children “When Our verses are recited to him, he says, Legends of the ancients” and this is the more apparent of the two aspects, and the other is that it is intended by it, Because he had wealth and children, you would obey him, as a rebuke to whoever obeyed him, and after the rest of the reciters of Madinah, Kufa and Basra recited it:إن كان ذ مالas a statement without a question with one hamza, and its meaning if it is recited like that: And do not obey every humiliating oath-taker “if he had wealth and children” as if he forbade him from obeying him because he had wealth and children.

x: And His saying,
h
When Our verses are recited to him
, he says, ‘Legends of the ancients.’ He says: When the verses of Our Book are recited to him, he says, This is from what the ancients wrote, mocking him and denying that it was from God.
And his saying:
h
We will brand him on the snout
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: We will brand him with the sword, and we will make that a lasting mark and a permanent mark on him as long as he lives.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
We will brand him on the snout
. So he fought on the day of Badr, and he was cut off with the sword in the battle.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: We will make it something lasting.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying,
h
We will brand him on the snout
is a shin that does not leave the last letter on it.

x: Others said: It will be marked on his nose.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
We will brand him on the snout

. He said: We will brand him on the nose. The more correct of the two interpretations of this, in my opinion, is the one that says: The meaning of this is: We will make his matter clear so that they will know him, and it will not be hidden from them, just as the mark on the snout is not hidden. Qatada said: The meaning of this is: A disgrace that cannot be surpassed by the last thing on him. It may also be possible that he was struck by the sword, so the striking of the snout by the sword was combined with the explanation of his faults to the people. And by his saying We will brand him he means we will cauterize him.

x: Some of them said: The meaning of that is: We will brand him with the mark of the people of Hellfire, meaning we will blacken his face. He said: Even though the nose is specifically mentioned as a mark, it is in the manner of the face, because some parts of the face lead to others. The Arabs say: By God, I will brand you with a mark that will not leave you, meaning the nose. He said: And some of them recited to me: I will brand him with a mark that will never leave him, just as the brand burns with the heat of the hottest day. Al-Najz: a disease that affects camels, so their noses are cauterized.

God Almighty means by His statement, Indeed, We tested them, that is, We tested the polytheists of Quraysh. He says: We examined them and tried them. As We tested the companions of the garden, that is, as We tested the companions of the garden. When they swore to harvest it in the morning, that is, when they swore to harvest some of its fruit in the morning.
And they do not make an exception: They do not say, God willing. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Hannad bin Al-Sarri told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding His statement, No poor person shall enter it upon you today, he said: They were people from Abyssinia whose father had a garden from which he used to feed the poor. When their father died, his sons said, By God, our father was truly foolish when he fed the poor. So they swore that they would harvest it in the morning and not make any exceptions, nor would they feed a poor person.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement, They will surely harvest it in the morning, he said: Paradise belonged to an old man, and he used to give charity. His sons used to forbid him from giving charity, but he used to hold back his sustenance for the year and spend and give charity from the excess. When their father died, they went to it in the morning and said, No poor person should enter it upon you today. He mentioned that the people of Paradise were people of the Book.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told us, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement, Indeed, We tested them as We tested the companions of the garden when they swore... the verse. He said: They were from the People of the Book. And severing means cutting. What is meant by his statement, that they may harvest it is that they may find its fruit. And from this is the statement of Imru’ al-Qais: I cut you off after Daad contacted me and Daad started to feel some anger

x: God Almighty says: A visitor from God’s command knocked on the door of these people’s paradise at night while they were asleep. In Arabic, the word tourist only occurs at night, and not during the day. They might say: I visited it during the day. Al-Farra’ mentioned that Abu Al-Jarrah recited to him: She extinguished it during the day and not at night, and her Lord was distracted by the pursuit of the camels. Rakhaal: are the female offspring of sheep. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about the meaning of that.
Who said that?

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kurayb told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: I asked Ibn Abbas about the flood: And a group from your Lord swept over it. He said: It is a command from God.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And a company from your Lord circulated around them while they were asleep
. He said: A company from God circulated around them while they were asleep.

x: And his statement,
h
So it became like a barren field
The people of interpretation differed as to what was meant by barren field.
Some of them said: It meant the black night.
Some of them said: The meaning of that is: So their garden became burnt and black like the blackness of a dark, pitch-black night.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Sahl bin Askar told me, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Our sheikh told us, on the authority of sheikhs from the tribe of Kalb,
m: whose name was Sulayman, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement,
h
So it became like a barren land

, he said: Barren land means night. x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: It became like a land called Al-Sareem, known by this name.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Na’im ibn Abd al-Rahman told me that
m: he heard Sa’id ibn Jubayr say: It is a land in Yemen called Dharwan, six miles from Sana’a.

Go to your tillage and that crop if you are harvesters he says: if you are harvesters of your crops.

That no poor person shall enter it today upon you. He says: And they whispered to each other, saying: That no poor person shall enter your Paradise today upon you.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, And they called one another in the morning, ‘Go forth to your tillage if you should be sharp-shooters.’ So they went while they spoke in low tones, meaning, they whispered, that no poor person should enter it upon you today.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: When their father died, they went to her and said: No poor person should enter her today.

Who said that?

m: regarding his statement,
h
And they went forth in the morning

h
And they set out in the morning

m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, on hardship, able, on hardship, able in themselves.

Who said that?

m: h
And they set out in the morning
, with great determination. He said: Their father had a field, and they were brothers, so they said: We will not feed a poor person from it until we know what comes out of it.
h
And they set out in the morning
, with great determination, on a matter that they had established among themselves.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, on a stubborn matter, he said: on a matter that is agreed upon.

m: h
And they set out in the morning
, determined and able. He said: On a matter of consensus.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: They became poor and needy.

h
And they set out in the morning

x: Others said: Rather, it means: with anger.
Who said that?
