m: h
And they set out in the morning

with great anger and power. He said: With wrath. It seems that Sufyan went in his interpretation of this to something like the saying of Al-Ashab bin Ramila: Blacks bought and found hidden blacks, they fell on the lions’ blood Meaning: in anger.

i: Some of the people of Al-Ma’ufa, who spoke Arabic from Basra, interpreted this as, They went out to prevent, and he directed it to the fact that it is from their saying: Haradat Al-Sana if there was no rain in it, and Haradat Al-Naqah if she had no milk, as the poet said:
x: If she is angry or cries, turn away from another eyebrow and cover it with mud.

This is a statement that we do not know of anyone from among the early scholars who said it, even if it has a basis. If that is the case and it is not permissible for us to go beyond what the evidence has agreed upon, then the only valid statement on that is one of the statements we mentioned from the people of knowledge. If that is the case, and what is known of the meaning of hard in the speech of the Arabs is the intention, from their saying: So-and-so has haraded so-and-so has haraded: if he intended his intention, and from that is the saying of the rajaz poet: And a flood came, which was from the command of God, and it raged like the raging of the enslaved Paradise. Meaning: He intended to intend it. It is true that the one who is more deserving of the interpretation of the verse is the one who said: The meaning of his saying and they went out in the morning with great determination is that they went out with a matter that they had intended and relied on, and kept it secret among themselves, capable of it in themselves.
God Almighty says: When these people reached their garden and saw its crops burned, they denied it and doubted it, whether it was their garden or not.

Some of them said to their companions, thinking that they had forgotten the path to their garden and that the one they had seen was another: We, O people, have lost our way to our garden. One of them, who knew that it was their garden and that they had not strayed from the path, said: Rather, we, O people, are deprived. We have been deprived of the benefit of our garden by the loss of its crops. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So when they saw it, they said, ‘Indeed, we are astray.’ That is, we have lost our way.

x: Rather, we are deprived. Rather, we were rewarded, so we were deprived.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So when they saw it, they said, ‘Indeed, we are astray.’ Qatada said: They said, “We have lost our way. This is not our Paradise.”

x: Some of them said, Rather, we are deprived. We have been deprived of our Paradise.
And his saying: He said the most just of them means: the most just of them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
The most just of them said
, he said, The most just of them, and it is said, The best of them said, and he said in Al-Baqarah, And thus We have made you a just community (al-Baqarah 2:143), he said: The middle means justice.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
The most just of them said
, meaning: the most just of them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Furat bin Khallad told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: He said, ‘the most just of them’: the most just of them.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
The most moderate of them said
, he said: The most just of them.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id:
m: “He said: The most just of them.” He said: The most just of them.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
The most moderate of them said
, meaning the most just of them in speech, and he was the quickest of the people to panic, and the best of them in returning.
h
Did I not tell you
, why do you not glorify God?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “He said: The most just of them.” He said: The most just of them.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
The most just of them said
, meaning: The most just of them. And His saying,
h
Did I not tell you

, ‘Why do you not glorify God?’ He says: Why do you not make an exception when you say, We will surely triumph over it in the morning, and say, God willing. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Al-Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Why do you not glorify God? He said: It has reached me that it is an exception. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
Did I not tell you
, ‘Why do you not glorify God?’ He said: He says: You make an exception, so glorification was an exception for them.

x: God Almighty says: The companions of Paradise said: Glory be to our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers in our failure to make an exception in our division and our resolve not to feed the poor from the fruits of our Paradise.
And His statement,
h
So they turned to one another
, blaming one another, God Almighty says:
h
So they turned to one another
, blaming one another for their negligence in what they had neglected regarding the exception, and their determination to continue as they had been in not feeding the poor from their garden.
And His saying,
h
Woe to us
! We were indeed transgressors. He says: The people of Paradise said:
h
Woe to us
! We were indeed banished, disobeying God’s command by abandoning the exception and glorification.

God Almighty says, informing us of what the people of Paradise said: Perhaps our Lord will replace it for us with something better than it by our repentance for our previous wrongdoing, with something better than our Paradise. Indeed, we are desirous of our Lord. He says: Indeed, we are desirous of our Lord that He replace our Paradise, which has perished, with something better than it.
The Almighty said,
h
Such is the punishment

. The Almighty says, “As We did with the garden of the people of the garden, when it became like a dry land because of the calamity and corrupting plague We sent upon it, We did with those who disobeyed Our command and disbelieved in Our messengers in this immediate world. “And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater.” Meaning, the punishment of the Hereafter for those who disobeyed their Lord and disbelieved in Him is greater on the Day of Resurrection than the punishment and torment of this world. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, “
h
Such is the punishment
. And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew,” meaning by that the punishment of this world.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: God said,
h
Such is the punishment
, meaning the punishment of this world, and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
Such is the punishment

, he said: The punishment of this world, the destruction of their wealth: meaning the punishment of this world. His saying, If they had known, means: If these polytheists had known that God’s punishment for those who associate partners with Him is greater than His punishment for them in this world, they would have been deterred, repented, and turned back. But in doing so, they are ignorant and do not know.

x: God Almighty says: Indeed, for the righteous who fear God’s punishment by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins are with their Lord gardens of pleasure meaning: gardens of eternal pleasure.
And His statement,
h
Shall We then treat the Muslims like the criminals

? God Almighty says: Shall We treat, O people, those who submitted to Me in obedience, humbled themselves before Me in servitude, and were humble before My commands and prohibitions, in My honor and blessings in the Hereafter like the criminals who acquired sins, committed transgressions, and disobeyed My commands and prohibitions? No! God will not do that.

And His saying, What is the matter with you? How do you judge? Do you consider the obedient servant of God and the disobedient servant of God equal in their honor? God Almighty says: Do not treat them equally, for they are not equal before God. Rather, the obedient servant has permanent honor, and the disobedient servant has permanent humiliation.

God Almighty says to the polytheists of Quraysh 106:O people, by your equality between Muslims and criminals in the honor of God, do you have a book sent down from God, brought to you by a messenger from among His messengers, that you have what you choose, so that you may study in it what you say. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
Or have you a book in which you study
? He said: In it is what you say you read: you study it. And he recited, Or have We given them a book so they have clear evidence from it?
r
(Fatir 35:40)
... to the end of the verse.

x: And His statement, Indeed, you will have therein whatever you choose, God Almighty says: In that matter, you will have whatever you choose for yourselves. This is a command from God, a rebuke to these people and a rebuke to them for what they were saying of falsehood and what they were wishing for of false hopes.
And his saying,
h
Or do you have oaths from Us that will last until the Day of Resurrection

? He says: Do you have oaths from Us that will last until the Day of Resurrection, that you will have what you judge, meaning that you will have your judgment? But the alif was broken from in because the lam entered into al-Naba 78:meaning, do you have oaths from Us that you will have your judgment?

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Ask, O Muhammad, which of these polytheists has a firm oath against us by their rule until the Day of Resurrection? Leader means: guarantor of it. Among the Arabs, a leader is the guarantor and the one who speaks on behalf of the people.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
Which of them is responsible for
that? means:
h
Which of them is responsible for
that.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, Ask them
h
which of them is responsible for
that, he said:
h
Which of them is responsible for
that?

x: And His statement, Or do they have partners? Then let them produce their partners, if they are truthful. God Almighty says: Do these people have partners in what they say and describe of the matters that they claim are theirs? Then let them produce their partners in that, if they are truthful in what they claim of partners.
God Almighty says,
h
On the Day the shin will be laid bare
A group of the Companions and Followers of the Interpretation said: It will reveal a serious matter.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told me: Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Usama bin Zaid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: The day the shin will be uncovered. He said: It is a day of war and hardship.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
On the Day when the shin will be laid bare
. He said: About a great matter, like the poet’s saying:

c: The war started against us Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: h
On the Day when the shin will be laid bare

, and no believer will remain but will prostrate, and the back of the unbeliever will harden and become a single bone. Ibn Abbas used to say: A great matter will be laid bare. Haven’t you heard the Arabs say:

c: The war started against us Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
On the Day when the shin will be laid bare
, meaning: when the matter will be laid bare and the deeds will be made apparent, and its being laid bare: entering the Hereafter and the matter being laid bare from him.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
On the Day the shin will be laid bare
is the severe and terrifying matter of terror on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi and Ibn Hamid told me: Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
On the Day when the shin will be laid bare
, he said: The severity and seriousness of the matter. Ibn Abbas said: It is the most intense hour on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said:
m: The severity of the matter, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
On the Day when the shin will be laid bare

, he said: The severity of the matter, Ibn Abbas said: It is the first hour that will be on the Day of Resurrection, except that in the hadith of Al-Harith he said: And Ibn Abbas said: It is the most severe hour that will be on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim ibn Kulayb, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, who said:
m: About the severity of the matter.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
On the Day the shin will be laid bare
, he said: About a terrible and grave matter.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
On the Day the shin will be laid bare
, he said: On the Day the severity of the matter will be laid bare.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, On the Day when the shin will be uncovered, and Ibn Abbas used to say: The people of the Age of Ignorance used to say, War has rolled up its shin, meaning the coming of the Hereafter and the passing of this world. Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated: Abd al-Rahman narrated: Sufyan narrated: Salamah ibn Kuhayl narrated: Abu al-Zahra’ narrated: Abdullah said: God will appear to His creation on the Day of Resurrection until the Muslims pass by. He said: Then He will say: Who do you worship? They will say: We worship God and do not associate anything with Him. Then He will rebuke them two or three times, saying: Do you know your Lord? They will say: Our Lord. Then He will say: You were called to prostration while you were safe.

c: Yahya ibn Talha al-Yarbu'i narrated to me, saying: Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of al-Minhal ibn Amr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said:
m: A crier will call out on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:'Is it not just from your Lord, Who created you, then shaped you, then provided for you, then you turned away from Him, that He should appoint every servant among you as he appointed?' They will say: 'Yes.' He said: Then the gods they used to worship will be presented to every people, and they will tire them out and they will lead them to the Fire. But the people of the call will remain, and some of them will say to one another: 'What are you waiting for?' The people will go away, and they will say: 'We are waiting for Him to call us.' So He will come to them in a form.' He said: 'He will mention whatever God wills Surat al-Qalam 68:42
h
The Day the shin will be laid bare

and they will be called to prostrate, but they will not be able. of it, and He will reveal whatever He wills to reveal.' He said: 'They will fall down in prostration except for the hypocrites, for the backbone of their loins will become a single bone like the rumps of cows, and it will be said to them: 'Raise your heads toward your light.' Then he mentioned a long story.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Abu Bakr narrated to us, he said: Al-A'mash narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Qays ibn Sakin, he said:
m: Abdullah narrated to Umar while he was with him, On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds (al-Mutaffifin 83:6), he said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, he said: The people will stand before the Lord of the worlds for forty years, their eyes fixed on the heavens, barefoot and naked, bridled with sweat, and no human being will speak to them for forty years. Then a caller will call out: O mankind, is it not just from your Lord, who created you and shaped you and provided for you, then you worshipped other than Him, that He should give every people what they had taken? They said: Yes. He said: Then what they used to worship besides God will be presented to every people, meaning their gods, and they will follow them until they are thrown into the Fire, and only the Muslims and the hypocrites will remain. Then it will be said: Will you not go away, for the people have gone away? They will say: Until our Lord comes to us. He will say: And will you recognize Him? They said: If he confesses to us. He said: Then He will appear and those who used to worship Him will fall down in prostration. He said: And the hypocrites will remain, unable to do so, as if there are skewers on their backs. He said: Then He will take them and drive them to the Fire, and they will be thrown down, and these people will enter Paradise. He said: Then they will be met in Paradise with what they will be met with of reward, wives, and wide-eyed maidens. Each man of them will be in Paradise with such and such, between each Paradise is such and such, between the nearest and the farthest is a thousand years, and he will see the farthest as he sees the nearest. He said: And a man of good appearance will meet him, and if he looks at him coming, he will think that he is his Lord, and he will say to him: Do not do that, I am only your servant and your commander over a thousand villages. He said: Umar will say: O Ka’b, do you not hear what Abdullah is talking about? Ibn Jabalah narrated: Yahya ibn Hammad narrated: Abu Uwanah narrated: Sulayman al-A'mash narrated: Al-Munhal ibn Amr narrated: Abu Ubaydah and Qays ibn Sakn narrated: Abdullah said while he was speaking to Umar: Umar kept saying: Woe to you, Ka'b! Don't you hear what Abdullah is saying? When the people are gathered on their feet for forty years, their eyes fixed on the sky, no one will speak to them, and the sun will be over their heads until sweat bridles them, all of them righteous and wicked. Then a voice from the sky will call out: "O mankind, is it not just from your Lord, who created you, provided for you, and shaped you, then you turned away from other than Him, that every man among you should be given what he was given? They will say: "Yes." Then a voice from the sky will call out: "O mankind, let every nation set out to do what it used to worship." A mirage will be spread out for them. What they used to worship will be made visible to them. They will set out until they enter the Fire. Then it will be said to the Muslims: "What is holding you back?" They say: This is our place until our Lord comes to us. Then it is said to them: Will you recognize Him if you see Him? They say: If He confesses to us, we will recognize Him. He said: Abu Salih narrated from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that one of them would turn around and uncover his shin, and they would fall down in prostration. He said: The backs of the hypocrites will be fused together until they become a single bone, like the rumps of cows. He said: It will be said to them: Raise your heads to your light in proportion to your deeds. He said: A group of them will raise their heads to light like mountains, and they will pass over the Sirat like the blink of an eye. Then another group will raise their heads to things like palaces, and they will pass over the Sirat like the wind. Then others will raise before them things like houses, and they will pass like horses. Then others will be raised to a light less than that, and they will pull themselves up tightly, and others less than that will walk, until the last of the people will remain, a man on the tip of his toe like a lamp, and he will fall down one time and straighten up another time, and the fire will strike him and it will scatter from him until he comes out, and he will say: No one has been given what I have been given, and he does not know from what he was saved, except that I felt its touch, and I felt its heat. And he mentioned a long hadith, from which I have shortened this.

c: Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Ja'far ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to us, on the authority of Ata' ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call out: 'Let every nation join what it used to worship.' No one who used to worship an idol, a statue, or an image will remain, except that they will go until they fall into the Fire. Only those who used to worship God alone will remain, from the righteous and the wicked, and the dust of the People of the Book. Then Hell will be presented as if it were a mirage, one part crushing the other. Then the Jews will be called, and it will be said to them: 'What did you worship?' They will say: 'Uzair, the son of God.' He will say: 'You have lied. God has not taken a wife or a son. So what do you want?' They will say: 'O our Lord, we are thirsty.' He will say: 'Will you not then return?' They will go until they fall into the Fire. Then the Christians will be called, and it will be said: 'What did you worship?' They will say: 'The Messiah, the son of God.'" He will say, “You have lied. God has not taken a wife or a son. What do you want?” They will say, O our Lord, we are thirsty, give us something to drink. He will say, Will you not then be returned? They will go and fall into the Fire, and only those who used to worship God, both the righteous and the wicked, will remain. He said, “Then God will appear to us in a form other than the one in which we saw Him the first time, and He will say, ‘O people, every nation has followed what it used to worship, and you will remain.’ On that Day, none will speak to Him except the prophets. They will say, ‘We left the people in this world, and we were more in need of their company therein. Every nation has followed what it used to worship, and we are awaiting our Lord whom we used to worship.’ He will say, “I am your Lord.” They will say, We seek refuge in God from you. He will say, Is there a sign between you and God by which you recognize Him? They will say, Yes. He will uncover his shin, and they will all fall down in prostration. There will not remain anyone who had prostrated in this world for the sake of showing off, or showing off, or hypocrisy, except that his back will become a single plate. Every time he wants to prostrate, he will fall on his back. He will say, “Then he will return, raising up our righteous and our wrongdoers, and he will be equal to us in the form in which we saw him the first time. He will say, ‘I am your Lord.’ They will say, ‘Yes, you are our Lord,’” three times.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told me: My father and Saeed ibn al-Layth told me: Khalid ibn Yazid told us, on the authority of Abu Hilal, on the authority of Zaid ibn Aslam, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Saeed al-Khudri:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “His crier will call out and say: ‘Let every people join what they used to worship.’ So the people of the cross will go with their cross, and the people of idols with their idols, and the people of every god with their gods, until there remains whoever used to worship God, from the righteous and the wicked, and the remnants of the People of the Book. Then Hell will be brought forth and displayed as if it were a mirage.” Then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: Then we await our Lord. He said: If he said it, then the Almighty will come to them.

c: Then he told us
m: a hadith similar to the hadith of al-Masruqi.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman al-Maharibi narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Rafi’ al-Madani, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah,
m: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God will take revenge for the oppressed from the oppressor until no one remains accountable to anyone. Then God will appoint an angel from the angels in the image of Uzair, and the Jews will follow him. Then God will appoint an angel from the angels in the image of Jesus, and the Christians will follow him. Then a caller will call out that will be heard by all of creation, saying: ‘Let every people join their gods and what they used to worship besides God. ’ No one who used to worship anything besides God will remain without his gods being presented to him before him. Then they will be led to the Fire until no one remains except the believers, among whom are the hypocrites. Then God, the Most High, will say: ‘O people, the people have gone, the people have gone. Join your gods and what you used to worship. ’ They will say: ‘By God, we have no god but God, and we did not worship any god other than Him. ’ But it is God who made them steadfast. Then He will say to them a second time in the same way: ‘Join your gods and what you used to worship. ’” Do you worship? They will say the same, and it will be said: Is there a sign between you and your Lord that you recognize? They will say: Yes, and His greatness will be revealed to them, so that they will know that He is their Lord, and they will fall down on their faces in prostration before Him, and every hypocrite will fall on his back, and God will make their backs like the hooves of cows.”

c: Abu Zaid Umar ibn Shabah told me, saying: Al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, saying: Abu Saeed Ruh ibn Janah told us, on the authority of a client of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, on the authority of Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace:
h
On the Day the shin will be laid bare
, he said: On the Day of a great light, before which they will fall down in prostration.

c: Jaafar bin Muhammad Al-Bazuri told me: Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: regarding the statement of God,
h
On the Day the shin will be laid bare
, he said: The covering will be laid bare. He said: And they will be called to prostrate while they are safe.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Usamah ibn Zayd, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding His statement,
h
The Day the shin will be laid bare
, he said: It is a day of distress and hardship. It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he had read it as,
h
The Day the shin will be laid bare

, meaning: The Day the Resurrection will reveal severe hardship. The Arabs say, This matter was laid bare from the shin, if it became severe. From this comes the saying of the poet: She showed them her leg and it was clear that she was evil. His saying,
h
And they are called to prostrate
, but they are unable to do so, means: And they are called to uncover their shins in order to prostrate to God Almighty, but they are unable to do so.

evidence.text: It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he had read it as, The Day the shin will be laid bare, meaning: The Day the Resurrection will reveal severe hardship.

x: And His statement:
h
Their eyes will be humbled

, humiliation will cover them. He says: humiliation from the punishment of God will cover them. And they were called to prostrate while they were healthy. He says: And in this world, they were called to prostrate to Him while they were healthy, with nothing preventing them from doing so, and nothing standing between Him and them. It has been said: Prostration in this context is the obligatory prayer.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Taimi:
m: h
And they were called to prostration
while they were healthy. He said: To the obligatory prayer.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
And they were called to prostration

. He said: He hears the caller to the obligatory prayer but does not answer him. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Taymi,
h
And they were called to prostration
. He said: The obligatory prayer. And similar to what we said about His statement,
h
They are called to prostrate
, but they are unable... the verse, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement, And they used to be called to prostration while they were safe, he said: They are the disbelievers who used to call upon Him in this world while they were safe. So today He is calling upon them while they are afraid. Then God, the Exalted, informed us that He will stand between the polytheists and His obedience in this world and the Hereafter. As for in this world, He said, They could not hear, nor could they see
r
. As for the Hereafter, He said, So they cannot, * Their eyes will be downcast.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They will be called to prostrate

, but they will not be able to, that is, by God, on the Day of Resurrection. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “Permission will be given to the believers on the Day of Resurrection to prostrate, so the believers will prostrate, and among every believer will be a hypocrite, so the back of the hypocrite will harden from prostrating, and God will make the prostration of the believers towards them a rebuke, humiliation, degradation, regret, and sorrow.” His saying,
h
And they were called to prostration
, meaning in this world, and they were safe, meaning in this world.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: It has reached me that permission will be given to the believers on the Day of Resurrection to prostrate among every believer a hypocrite. The believers will prostrate, but the hypocrite will not be able to prostrate. I think he said: Their backs will harden, and the prostration of the believers will be a rebuke to them. He said: And they were called to prostrate while they were safe.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, I entrust the affair of these deniers of the Qur’an to Him. This is like someone saying to another person threatening a man: Leave me and him alone, meaning that he is behind his harm. Min in His statement,
h
And whoever denies this hadith

, is in the accusative case, because the meaning of the statement is what I mentioned. It is similar to their saying, If I left you to your own opinion, you would not succeed. The Arabs place the accusative case on your opinion because the meaning of the statement is: If I left you to your own opinion, you would not succeed. And His statement:
h
We will gradually lead them on from where they do not know

, God Almighty says: We will plot against them from where they do not know, by giving them enjoyment of worldly pleasures until they think that their enjoyment of them is better for them with God, so they persist in their transgression, then He will seize them suddenly while they do not perceive.

And His statement: “And I will grant them respite. Indeed, My plan is firm.” God Almighty says: And I will extend their terms for a period of time, and that is for a period of time, due to their disbelief and rebellion against God, so that God’s arguments against them may be complete. Indeed, My plan is firm. He says: Indeed, My plan against the people of disbelief is strong and severe.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, do you ask these polytheists for a reward and recompense for what you have given them of advice and called them to the truth? “They are burdened with a heavy fine. That is, they are burdened with the fine for that reward, and the burden of paying it has burdened them, so they refrained from accepting your advice and avoided, due to the great burden of the fine that had befallen them, and what you asked them for that was to enter into the religion to which you called them.

And His statement: Or do they have the unseen, so they write it down? He says: Do they have the Preserved Tablet, in which is the report of what will happen, so they write down what is in it, and argue with you about it, and claim that, despite their disbelief in their Lord, they have a better status with God than the people of faith in Him.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So be patient, O Muhammad, for the decree and judgment of your Lord concerning you and these polytheists, with what you have brought them of this Qur’an and this religion. Continue with what your Lord has commanded you to do, and do not let their denial of you and their harm to you prevent you from conveying what you have been commanded to convey. And His saying:
h
And do not be like the companion of the fish who was imprisoned in its belly
, and he is Jonah, son of Matta, peace be upon him, so your Lord will punish you for not conveying that, just as He punished him by imprisoning him in its belly
h
when he called out
while he was distressed meaning:
h
when he called out
while he was sad, and sadness had weighed him down and he was swallowing it.

c: As Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
When he called out
, full of grief, meaning: sorrowful.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Deeply distressed, he said: Sorrowful. Qatada used to say about his statement,
h
And do not be like the companion of the fish
,: Do not be like him in haste and anger.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So be patient over the decision of your Lord
h
and do not be like the companion of the fish
when he cried out in anguish. He said: Do not be hasty as he was hasty, and do not become angry as he became angry.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same.

x: And His saying:
h
Had it not been for the grace of his Lord overtaking him

, God Almighty says: Had it not been for the owner of the house overtaking a grace from his Lord, who had mercy on him with it, and accepted his repentance for his anger at his Lord, he would have been thrown into the open, which is the open space of the earth. And from this is the saying of Qays ibn Ja’dah: I raised my feet, not fearing their stumbling, and threw my clothes in the open country. And it is blameworthy.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his saying and it is blameworthy.
Some of them said: It means: and he is blameworthy.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told me, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, and he is blameworthy, he said: and he is blameworthy.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: He is guilty.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Bakr:
m: And he is blameworthy. He said: And he is a sinner.

x: God Almighty says: So his Lord chose the companion of the fish, meaning He selected him and chose him for his prophethood. And made him among the righteous, meaning among the messengers who acted according to what their Lord commanded them to do and refrained from what He forbade them from doing.

And His statement: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes God Almighty says: And indeed, O Muhammad, those who disbelieve would almost pierce you with their eyes because of the intensity of their enmity towards you and they would remove you and throw you when they look at you out of rage against you. It has been said that what is meant by that is: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost throw you, O Muhammad, and overthrow you, as the Arabs say: So-and-so almost overthrew me with the intensity of his looks at me. They said: The Quraysh only attacked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in order to cast the evil eye on him, so they looked at him to help him and said: We have never seen a man like him, or he is mad. So God said to His Prophet at that time: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost throw you with their eyes"
h
when they heard the message
and they say: He is mad.
And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of to make you slip, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement, And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the message, meaning: They would pierce you with their eyes from the intensity of their gaze. Ibn Abbas said: It is said of the aral-Saff 61:The arrow has slipped or slipped.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, that they may make you slip with their eyes, meaning: that they may make you slip with their eyes.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes, meaning: they would almost make you slip with their eyes.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: that he used to recite And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost destroy you.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, to make you slip, he said: to make you slip with their eyes.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement, to make you slip with their eyes, he said: to destroy you. Al-Kalbi said: to overthrow you.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes to pierce you with their eyes, in enmity towards the Book of God and the remembrance of God.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes, meaning: They would make you slip with their eyes out of enmity and hatred. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, li-zilaqunak. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it as li-zilaqunak with a fat-ha on the ya from zalatuhu zalqan. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it as li-zilaqunak with a damma on the ya from azlaquhu yazlaquhu. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings and two famous dialects among the Arabs, with similar meanings. The Arabs say to someone who shaves his head: he made him slip and he made him slip, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. And His statement:
h
When they heard the message

, meaning when they heard the Book of God being recited, and they say, ‘Indeed, he is mad,’ God Almighty says: These polytheists, whose characteristics He described, say, Muhammad is mad, and what he brought us is the delirium that he raves about in his madness.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, li-zilaqunak.
The majority of the reciters of Medina read it as li-zilaqunak with a fat-ha on the ya from zalatuhu zalqan.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it as li-zilaqunak with a damma on the ya from azlaquhu yazlaquhu.

x: And it is only a reminder to the worlds. Muhammad is only a reminder through which God reminded the two worlds, the jinn and mankind.

notes.en: The Companions disagreed on this question. Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah explained: “I have found that they—the Companions—disputed only over something like the saying of God Most High, ‘On the Day when the shin shall be uncovered’ [Q 68:42]. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās and a group that this refers to hardship: God will uncover the hardship of the Hereafter. Abū Saʿīd and a group counted it among the divine attributes, because of the report related by Abū Saʿīd in the two Ṣaḥīḥs. There is no doubt that the plain wording of the Qurʾān does not indicate that this is one of the attributes, for it says, ‘when a shin shall be uncovered,’ using an indefinite noun in an affirmative statement; it does not attribute the shin to God Most High or say ‘His shin.’ Without definiteness through possessive attribution, it is not apparent that this is an attribute unless there is some other evidence. This is not the kind of interpretation [that would be considered figurative exegesis] …” Majmūʿ al-fatāwā (6/394–395).
notes.ar: هذه المسألة اختلف فيها الصحابة رضي الله عنهم، وقد بين ذلك شيخ الإسلام ابن تيمية قائلًا: إني لم أجدهم -أى الصحابة- تنازعوا إلا في مثل قوله تعالى: {يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَنْ سَاقٍ} فروى عن ابنِ عباس وطائفة أن المراد به الشدة، أن الله يكشف عن الشدة فى الآخرة، وعن أبي سعيد وطائفة أنهم عدُّوها في الصفات؛ للحديث الذي رواه أبو سعيد في الصحيحين، ولا ريب أن ظاهر القرآن لا يدل على أن هذه من الصفات، فإنه قال: {يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَنْ سَاقٍ} نكرة فى الإثبات، لم يضفها إلى الله تعالى، ولم يقل: عن ساقه، فمع عدم التعريف بالإضافة لا يظهر أنه من الصفات إلا بدليل آخر، ومثل هذا ليس بتأويل. . . مجموع الفتاوى 6/ 394، 395.

notes.en: T1 reads “layaltafit”; Ibn Mandah’s al-Īmān reads “yanqalib” (“turn back”), which may be correct. The meaning is that one of them almost turns away and retreats from what is right because of the severe trial that took place. God knows best. See Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim (no. 183/302).
notes.ar: في ت 1: "ليلفت"، وفى الإيمان لابن منده: "ينقلب"، ولعله الصواب؛ والمعنى: يكاد أحدهم ينصرف ويرجع عن الصواب للامتحان الشديد الذى جرى. والله أعلم. وينظر صحيح مسلم (183/ 302).

notes.en: M reads “kamurr”; T2, “kajīr”; T3, “kajayyid.” Al-ḥaḍr is a horse’s lift as it runs; a miḥḍār is a horse that runs swiftly. Al-Tāj, root ḥ-ḍ-r.
notes.ar: في م: "كمر"، وفي ت 2: "كجير"، وفى ت 3: "كجيد". والحضر: ارتفاع الفرس في عَدْوِه، وفرس مِحْضار: شديد العدو. التاج (ح ض ر).

notes.en: Al-shadd means “running at a gallop.” Lisān al-ʿArab, root sh-d-d.
notes.ar: الشد: العَدْو. اللسان (ش د د).

notes.en: Shaʿithtu min al-ṭaʿām means “I ate a little food.” Lisān al-ʿArab, root sh-ʿ-th.
notes.ar: شَعِثْتُ من الطعام: أكلت قليلا. اللسان (ش ع ث).

notes.en: Ghubarāt is the plural of ghubbar; ghubar is the plural of ghābir, and ghābir means “what remains.” Al-Nihāyah (3/338).
notes.ar: غبرات: جمع غُبَّر، والغبر: جمع غابر، والغابر: الباقي. النهاية 3/ 338.

notes.en: Muslim transmitted it (no. 183/303). Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim in al-Sunnah (no. 635) and ʿAbd Allāh in al-Sunnah (no. 429) transmitted abbreviated versions. It was also transmitted by Ibn Khuzaymah in al-Tawḥīd (p. 200), Abū ʿAwānah in his Musnad (1/166–168), Ibn Naṣr in Taʿẓīm qadr al-ṣalāh (no. 277), and Ibn Mandah in al-Īmān (no. 816) and al-Radd ʿalā al-jahmiyyah (no. 1), as well as al-Ḥākim (4/582–584), through Jaʿfar ibn ʿAwn. Aḥmad (17/202–204, no. 11127), al-Bukhārī (no. 4581), and Muslim (no. 183/302) transmitted it through Zayd ibn Aslam.
